tools.name: search-events
tools.description: Search upcoming published events on Pandy Tickets in Guatemala, soonest first, 20 per page. Each result has its public URL, dates, venue, how people get in (free, transfer or card) and the lowest price.

tools.name: get-event
tools.description: One published event: description, ticket types with prices and whether each is sold out, what the registration form asks, and how people get in (entry.url and Spanish entry.instructions to relay).

tools.name: get-checkout-link
tools.description: The link a person opens to buy tickets or register, with Spanish instructions to relay. For paid events (card or bank transfer), checkout opens with the ticket type and quantity already chosen. For free registration, it is the event page. Nothing is reserved or charged: the person completes it thems

tools.name: draft-event
tools.description: Prepare a person's own event on Pandy Tickets from what they told you (name, date, place, ticket categories with price and quantity). Nothing is published and no account is created: it returns a one-time claim_url, valid 48 hours. The person opens it, signs in with Google, and lands on a screen wher

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search-events, get-event, get-checkout-link · Public sink: draft-event.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search-events, get-event, get-checkout-link · Public sink: draft-event

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "draft-event" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
